editorial:
In 1984, a group of young LGBT activists in London decide to raise money for striking coal miners in Wales. The miners are struggling, and the activists want to help. But when they try to donate, the Union is too embarrassed to accept their support. So the activists take matters into their own hands and travel to a small mining village to meet the workers face to face. What follows is a funny, warm, and moving story about two very different groups learning to stand together. The movie balances big laughs with real heart, showing how unlikely friendships can change lives on both sides.

The acting is fantastic across the board, with standout performances that make you care about every character. The pacing keeps things lively without rushing the emotional beats. Some moments lean a bit sentimental, but the humor keeps it grounded. If you enjoy feel-good stories about community and courage, this one is for you. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the miners show up at the London Pride parade to support the activists, returning the solidarity they received. The village that once rejected the group now proudly marches alongside them. It is a powerful reversal that shows how much has changed. The movie ends on a hopeful note, celebrating unity and the idea that standing together makes everyone stronger.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves feel-good stories about community and unlikely friendships.
